label: copy-phase input r (echoing original position >= 2)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the token r is fed back as input during the copy phase (in_tok r accounts for 100% of activation mass; never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on r in the original sequence). It requires the echoed r to be original token 2 or later (recall_idx >= 3); r echoed from original positions 0-1 gives no or weak activation (recall_idx 2 rate 0.7%, recall_idx<=1 zero). Magnitude increases with copy position: the strongest activations (~5) are r near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1), and early-copy r gives weak activations (lowest-quartile examples). Does not depend on output token, next token, first token, or L beyond this position effect. Simple predicate in_tok==r in copy phase gives F1 0.78 (precision 0.65) because of early-copy r.

issues: The reported test scores reproduce: precision 0.961, recall 0.941, F1 0.951, mass recall 0.975 on the test split. The claims about phase and token also hold: the feature is silent in the original and delimiter phases, and in_tok r carries 100% of the activation mass.

There is one systematic miss class, not scattered noise. An echoed r from original position 1 (recall_idx == 2) fires almost every time in short sequences. Precision of copy-phase r at recall_idx 2 is 1.00 for L=3 (423 steps) and 0.99 for L=4 (2455 steps), but 0.15 for L=5 and 0.00 for L>=6. These steps make up most of the 3489 test misses. Misses output shows examples like 'z r d 0 <DEL> z [r:0.23]' and 'p r 0 <DEL> p [r:0.47]'.

The explanation says the rate is 0.7% at recall_idx 2. That is the base rate across all input tokens. Among echoed r at recall_idx 2 the rate is about 20%, and close to 100% when the r is near the end of the copy (to_go <= 1). So the cutoff depends on distance to the end of the copy, not only on original position.

The fixed position boundary also gives systematic false positives. An echoed r from original position 2 (recall_idx 3) in long sequences fires less often: precision 0.61 at L=8 and 0.68 at L=9, against 1.00 for L<=6. These are cases with to_go 4-5, and most of the 2279 test false positives look like this, e.g. 'n i r l 1 2 h d <DEL> n i *r*'.

So the label 'echoing original position >= 2' overclaims a hard position cutoff. The real condition mixes position and to_go: the feature fires on echoed r unless it is early in the copy, i.e. high to_go together with low recall_idx. This fits the profile, where activation is zero at to_go >= 6.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input r, except early in the copy (fires when the echoed r is from original position >= 2 or is within the last two copy steps)
